text: Stop. You use ITC products every day, but seventy four percent of its profit comes from cigarettes.
Think about your day. Aashirvaad atta for chapati. Dark Fantasy with tea. Bingo chips. Yippee noodles.
A Classmate notebook for school. Savlon and Fiama in the bathroom. Mangaldeep in the pooja room. All ITC.
So how does ITC actually make its money?

Last quarter, cigarettes brought in fifteen thousand five hundred crore of gross revenue. Other FMCG, nearly seven thousand crore, up sixteen percent. Agri, forty four hundred crore. Paper, three thousand crore.
But look at the profit. About seventy four percent still comes from cigarettes. FMCG is just eleven percent.
And this quarter, profit fell twenty percent, to four thousand one hundred crore, after cigarette taxes went up in February.
So ITC is betting big on everything else. A twenty thousand crore investment push. New brands like twenty four Mantra, Yoga Bar and Prasuma. And it just bought Century Pulp and Paper.
The stock? About two hundred seventy nine rupees. Roughly thirty three percent below its fifty two week high.
Will FMCG ever beat cigarettes? Follow for part two.
